en: Because he grants fearlessness out of affection, because he extinguishes the suffering of the distressed, because of his magnanimity, because he dries up sins, and because he leads one to the state of unsurpassed bliss—
Śrīpati alone is to be served; these [deities] have become witnesses to this.
And Prahlāda, Vibhīṣaṇa, Karirāj, Pāñcālya, Ahalyā, and Dhruva. || 1 ||
"O Prahlāda, if there is a Lord named Hari, show him to me everywhere;
show him even in this pillar! As the asura was speaking thus, Hari appeared there, rending his chest with his own claws and manifesting his affection.
The Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa, who is solely intent on protecting those in distress—he is my refuge. || 2 ||
"Śrī Rāma is here; this Vibhīṣaṇa, free from sin, has arrived out of fear of the Rākṣasas.
Sugrīva, bring him and protect him now, for he has come as a descendant of Pulastya.
Having spoken thus, Rāghava granted him universal renown and freedom from fear.
The Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa, who is solely devoted to protecting those in distress, is my refuge. || 3 ||
When the gods, including Brahmā and the rest, were powerless before him as he uttered piteous cries— saying, "O gods, protect me!"— with his feet seized by a crocodile and his hands raised up;
then the wielder of the discus, Śrīdhara, [cried out] to him, "Do not fear," while slaying that crocodile.
That Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa, who is solely intent on protecting those in distress, is my refuge. || 4 ||
"O Kṛṣṇa, O Acyuta! O Abode of Mercy, O Hari! O Friend of the Pāṇḍavas!
Where are you? Where are you? Protect me, who am distressed and being carried away by Suyodhana!"—thus addressed, he whose body was clothed in imperishable garments protected Draupadī.
The Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa, who is solely devoted to protecting those in distress, is my refuge. || 5 ||

The water from the toenails of whose lotus-feet destroys the flood of sins of the three worlds, and the nectar of whose name, when drunk by those who partake of it, carries them across the ocean of saṃsāra;
even a stone was liberated from the curse of a sage by the dust of the mud of whose feet.
That Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa, who is solely intent on protecting those in distress, is my refuge. || 6 ||
Having seen his brother seated upon the supreme throne, Dhruva, the son of Uttānapāda, desiring to ascend to that very height, suffered great humiliation from his mother;
yet, having gone to him for refuge, he obtained through penance the lion-throne of the golden mountain.
The Blessed Lord Nārāyaṇa, who is solely devoted to protecting those in distress, is my refuge. || 7 ||
Afflicted, despondent, weary, and terrified, even while beset by terrible diseases, those who merely chant the name "Nārāyaṇa" become freed from suffering and attain happiness. (8)
Thus ends the Nārāyaṇāṣṭaka composed by the venerable Kūreśasvāmin.
